sections.name: Hydrogen Peroxide, Heavy Water & Hydrogen Economy

statements.label: Statement I
statements.text: Hydrogen peroxide can act as an oxidising agent as well as a reducing agent in both acidic and alkaline media.

statements.label: Statement II
statements.text: In the reaction of H₂O₂ with acidified KMnO₄, the oxidation state of oxygen changes from −1 in H₂O₂ to −2 in the liberated oxygen gas.

options: Both Statement I and Statement II are correct.
Both Statement I and Statement II are incorrect.
Statement I is correct but Statement II is incorrect.
Statement I is incorrect but Statement II is correct.
questions.explanation: Statement I is correct. Statement II is incorrect because in reducing reactions of H₂O₂, oxygen is oxidised from −1 (in H₂O₂) to 0 in elemental O₂(g).
questions.ncert: "It acts as an oxidising as well as reducing agent in both acidic and alkaline media." 2MnO₄⁻ + 6H⁺ + 5H₂O₂ → 2Mn²⁺ + 8H₂O + 5O₂

statements.label: Assertion (A)
statements.text: Containers of hydrogen peroxide must be kept completely free of dust particles.

statements.label: Reason (R)
statements.text: Dust particles can catalyse and induce explosive decomposition of hydrogen peroxide into water and oxygen.

options: Both (A) and (R) are true and (R) is the correct explanation of (A).
Both (A) and (R) are true but (R) is not the correct explanation of (A).
questions.explanation: Both (A) and (R) are true, and (R) provides the exact reason given in the text.
questions.ncert: "It is kept away from dust because dust can induce explosive decomposition of the compound."
